analysis.title: Wrapping up TMT 2026 – Welcome to the Agentic World
key_insights: European software AI roadmaps have matured versus last year's conference, with clearer agentic functionality. MS sees this as supportive of medium-term growth, with industry view In-Line.

SAP outlines an autonomous enterprise with agents across Finance, HR and other workflows. Dassault sees virtual companions for Engineering and Life Sciences. Wolters Kluwer's Libra extends proprietary legal content into AI drafting and workflow tools.
Investors will want proof that AI is turning into incremental revenue. MS expects AI revenue to be more of a 2H27 than 1H27 story in general.
SAP plans to introduce a dedicated AI-related revenue KPI in January 2027, which MS sees as a positive step for building confidence in the AI opportunity.

Pricing is moving beyond seats. Dassault uses Blue tokens charged on outputs, Nemetschek plans subscriptions plus consumption credits for Max products, and SAP uses committed consumption for spend predictability.

RELX targets around 20% capture of the value it creates for customers. Accenture sees growth in outcome-based contracts, and Capgemini sees room to expand fixed-price engagements as AI improves delivery efficiency.

Management teams are more open about AI lowering cost bases. SAP expects headcount to decline, Amadeus believes it can grow with its current employee base, and Dassault expects AI to halve incremental hiring without cutting its workforce.
Sage announced a c. £100m restructuring charge with FY26 results this week, with a small net headcount reduction. IONOS in September targeted a c. 12% workforce reduction.

MS thinks CFO concerns about token costs have subsided versus earlier in the year. The open debate is whether opex efficiency can drive EBIT margin expansion against gross-margin pressure from AI compute and partner payments.

Mistral and Databricks argue model intelligence is a shrinking constraint and differentiation comes from data, customisation and cost-efficient deployment. Databricks is expanding into agentic applications, raising the question of whether value accrues to incumbents or independent platforms.

market_movers.rationale: Autonomous enterprise vision, committed-consumption pricing and a new AI revenue KPI due January 2027 support the AI case. Headcount expected to decline.

sector_views.rationale: Industry view In-Line. AI product strategies and productivity evidence are encouraging, but revenue proof-points are more likely 2H27.

risk_factors: AI revenue may arrive later than investors expect, more 2H27 than 1H27.

tension_points.bear_case: Higher AI computing costs and partner payments could create gross-margin headwinds that offset opex efficiency.

tension_points.bear_case: Independent platforms such as Databricks that assemble multi-system data and context could capture the value instead.
